_provenance_playwright: Browser reads flow for the Operator; browser writes ask. The ten write-shaped browser tools (click, drag, drop, evaluate, file_upload, fill_form, handle_dialog, press_key, select_option, type) each carry an exact-name ask rule. The read-shaped tools carry no rule of their own. The guard-live-reads.sh PreToolUse hook lets a call through to the auto-mode classifier only when the Operator makes it and the tool is on the hook's read list; it asks on a call from the main session or any other agent, and on any browser tool the list does not name. navigate and navigate_back are on the read list, so a URL the Operator opens is not prompted. Two deny rules, the glob browser_run_code* and the exact browser_run_code_unsafe, block the RCE-class code-execution tool outright. The glob covers current and legacy tool names (nothing else shares the prefix), and the exact string guarantees a match for the pinned tool version (mid-name glob behavior is undocumented). The ask rules, the denies and the hook's read list re-verify against the enumerated tool inventory on every version move.
_provenance_claude_ai_connectors: The claude.ai account-connector rules are a layered set: reads flow for the Operator, writes ask. The guard-live-reads.sh PreToolUse hook sees every connector tool. It lets a call through silently to the auto-mode classifier only when the Operator makes it and the tool is on the hook's read list (the Gmail search, get and list tools; the Drive search, list, read, metadata, permissions and download tools), and asks on everything else: a write, a call from the main session or any other agent, a tool of a connector no curation has admitted, a tool upstream adds later, and input the hook cannot parse. The exact-string Gmail and Drive ask entries name every known write tool, so a write still asks if the hook ever fails to run; exact strings are also startup typo-check tripwires (glob rules are exempt from the startup check, exact strings are not, and a mismatch surfaces a warning). The deny entries are TRIPWIRES, not boundaries: mcp__claude_ai_Google_Calendar__* and mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__* deny two un-curated connector classes wholesale; Gmail send*/delete* and Drive share*/delete* pre-empt name-prefixed destructive and exfil tools absent from the connector's toolset as enumerated at admission; the deny is a tripwire should upstream ever add them, and the drift shows when it bites. The reply, forward and trash tools the connectors expose match none of those prefixes: they are writes, and they ask by exact name. No allow rules by decision; a read that flows is decided by the classifier, never auto-allowed. The ask rules, the denies and the hook's read list re-verify against the live inventory at every deploy and every re-enumeration. Operator confinement is doctrinal, not structural; the deny/ask layer and the hook are the structural carrier.
_provenance_model_and_remote_control: Two settings pairs control the model default and Remote Control's startup behavior. 'model' is set to the 'opus' alias, so it always tracks whatever build the alias currently resolves to. 'modelSettings' sets effortLevel to 'medium' under two keys: 'opus' and 'claude-opus-5'. The alias key is what the harness's alias resolver actually applies, since modelSettings keys are normalized through that resolver; the full-model-ID key stays declared so a later deploy never prunes the value from a host that still carries it. If an effort level is later saved through '/effort' for a specific model, the harness stores it under that model's own canonical ID, and a canonical-ID key always takes precedence over an alias key, so a saved choice is never overridden by this file. 'remoteControlAtStartup' is false, so the Remote Control bridge does not start itself each session, while the in-session toggle, the claude.ai/code route, and the --remote-control flag all stay available. 'disableRemoteControl' is deliberately not set, since that key would remove those manual routes too. These are user-level settings: repo-scoped (project or local) settings cannot enable Remote Control, and both keys are read from the merged settings across all tiers, so this file's values take effect once deployed.
_provenance_auto_compact_window: autoCompactWindow sets how full the context gets before Claude Code compacts on its own: 400,000 tokens, for every model. Unset, a model with a native 1M window compacts at about 967K, and a session that large re-sends its whole history with every turn; 400,000 is the backstop under that, while a manual /compact with a stated focus, or a fresh session, stays the working refocus. Claude Code caps the value at the model's window, so a smaller model compacts at its own limit. Overrides, highest first: the CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW variable, then the --autocompact flag for one launch, then a window saved with /autocompact, which lives under modelSettings for the current model and wins over this key for that model. A deploy writes this single value from the factory and leaves a per-model window alone, since this file declares none; a host that wants its own value for every model names autoCompactWindow in settings.optout.json. An automatic compaction is never blocked: the refocus hook under hooks.PreCompact stops only a manual /compact.
_provenance_claude_md_excludes: claudeMdExcludes keeps instruction files this COS does not ship out of sessions that reach this home through the Agent SDK, such as T3 Code's. Those sessions set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR to this home but keep the SDK's default setting sources (user, project and local), so the loader walks up from the working folder and loads, as project memory, the user's own ~/.claude instruction files (that folder is an ancestor of most working folders) and, inside a clone of this COS's source, the source copy of this home's CLAUDE.md. Only instruction files arrive that way: settings, skills, plugins and hooks under ~/.claude do not reach such a session. Three patterns cover the user's own ~/.claude: any user folder under a Users directory (Windows and macOS), any Linux user home, and root's home. Matching is case-sensitive against a path built from the working folder as the host spells it, so each letter of the Users segment is a class of both its cases ([Uu] and so on), and a lowercase or uppercase spelling of the same folder still matches, where an exact pattern did not (case variants tested on Windows, the Linux home pattern in WSL, on 2.1.296). The fourth names always-on/CLAUDE.md under cos/ensemble-claude-code, the file this home's CLAUDE.md is deployed from, so a session working in a clone of the source does not load the source copy beside the deployed one. Nested files, loaded as Claude works in a subfolder, honor the patterns, AGENTS.md included. Such sessions also read project settings, and the claudeMdExcludes lists of all settings layers add up, so a repository keeps its own instruction files out with the same key in its own .claude/settings.json. Launcher sessions are unaffected: under --setting-sources user they load only this home's own instruction files, which no pattern matches. This home must not be ~/.claude itself: the home patterns would then match its own CLAUDE.md and rules and strip them from every session.
_provenance_env: env sets PYTHONUTF8=1 for every session and its subprocesses, so Python runs in UTF-8 mode: open() without an encoding reads and writes UTF-8 rather than the Windows ANSI code page (cp1252 on Western European systems), which raises UnicodeEncodeError on any character outside it, an arrow for one. It changes nothing where the locale is already UTF-8. It is one single value: the merge writes it from the factory, leaves every other env key the host sets (ENSEMBLE_BROWSER among them) alone, and a host that wants its own value names env.PYTHONUTF8 in settings.optout.json.
_provenance_plugin_install_asks: Forty of the ask rules make Claude ask before its own shell installs, enables or scaffolds a plugin: claude plugin install, claude plugin enable and claude plugin init in every spelling claude plugin --help lists on 2.1.287 (plugin or plugins, install or i, init or new; enable has no alias), ten prefixes, each bare and with arguments (the form of the git push rules), for Bash and for PowerShell. The bare rule stays beside the one with arguments: the permissions page says a trailing space and * also match the bare command, which is untested for the PowerShell tool, and the git push rules rely on the pair. A plugin can carry a mod, a hooks module whose tool.check or tool.call hook can approve a tool call past the ask rules, deny rules and guards this file wires (HARNESS.md), so these three commands get a prompt. What they cannot catch: they match the command text Claude writes, so a flag before plugin, a path-qualified claude, a nested shell, an alias a later version adds and a letter-case variant such as CLAUDE plugin install (this host's Git Bash runs it as the same program, and on 2.1.287 a Bash rule did not catch CLAUDE plugin i where it caught claude plugin i, observed; the permissions page says PowerShell rule matching ignores case, unprobed here) pass them, and a mod already loaded can approve past an ask rule. The user's own installs never meet them: /plugin, a plugin synced from the account, a plugin folder put into skills/, the --plugin-dir flag and CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS. The mod-presence check under hooks.SessionStart (session-start-mod-check.sh) reports a mod at the next session start however it arrived, except one loaded with --plugin-dir.

PreToolUse._provenance_herenow_gate: Wires the here.now gate onto every Bash and PowerShell call, for every caller. here.now site and Drive writes are live external writes, a hard human gate; a publish is owner-only by default, the kit locking and checking it. For the Operator (top-level agent_type 'operator') the gate is an allowlist: its shell runs the kit tools/herenow.sh and nothing else; check, manifest and the site and Drive reads (site-ls, site-files, site-cat, drive-ls, drive-cat) pass on to the classifier; a publish or drive-put marked --ordered, the dispatch quoting the human's order, passes when its target or local file lies inside the session's root (judged by guard-archivist-paths.sh main-session) and asks outside it or when that check could not be made; an unflagged publish or drive-put asks, naming the act; a --public publish always asks; and every other command, a PowerShell call included, is blocked with the accepted forms printed. For every other caller a command carrying a here.now publish, site, Drive or key shape (publish.sh, drive.sh, here.now/api, HERENOW_API_KEY, HERENOW_DRIVE_TOKEN, .herenow/credentials, herenow.sh publish, herenow.sh site-, herenow.sh drive-) asks, and everything else passes. Never a pass on an unfinished check: an EXIT trap and position guards turn every internal failure into a block for the Operator and an ask for everyone else, and the 30-second timeout is set explicitly (one path-guard run at most; a check call measured about 1.3 s on the host it was built on). What that cannot cover: a hook that cannot start at all still fails open. No permissions.ask entry backs this gate: the design kept one only where a scratch probe showed a Bash rule carrying quotes and $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR matching the command text, and the probe could not run (a scratch config home has no login, and a probe through the live home would write into it), so the gate is the sole mechanical carrier and the Operator card's confirm-first the doctrinal one.

PreToolUse._provenance_cross_shell_nudge: Wires the cross-shell nudge onto every Bash and PowerShell call, for every caller. The first time an agent's command crosses a shell boundary (a nested interpreter: wsl, bash or sh -c, powershell or pwsh, cmd /c, ssh, docker exec or run; or, on Git Bash, a Windows python, py or node started from a Bash call), the hook adds one note beside the tool result: on Git Bash the host's two traps, the Bash tool halving backslash pairs and Windows Python failing on /c/ paths, then the pointer to load cross-shell-command-discipline before the next nontrivial crossing. A PreToolUse note lands after the command has run, so it serves the next crossing, not this one. Once per agent: an empty marker named for session_id plus agent_id (main when absent) in the temp folder, removed by the SessionEnd litter-flag hook. Quoted text and which, type, command -v and where lookups are dropped before matching, so an echo string or a grep pattern does not fire it. It never denies or asks and exits 0 on every path, a marker it cannot write meaning no note. Bash builtins only; the 5-second timeout bounds a hung start, since a command hook otherwise waits up to 600 seconds. Hooks on one matcher run in parallel, so it adds no wait beside the push gate and the here.now gate.

PreToolUse._provenance_delete_guard: Wires the delete guard onto every Bash and PowerShell call, for every caller, on the human's word. A member's command once ran find . ... -exec rm -rf after a clone failed and its cd was skipped, in the repository's root, and wiped the working tree; the card-and-doctrine hold that replaced the Examiner's retired Bash guard did not stop it, and the skill that teaches the guarded form had not been loaded. The guard asks, never denies, when the command text carries a tree-deleting or tree-resetting shape: rm with -r, find with -delete or -exec rm, xargs rm, git clean (not a dry run), git reset --hard, git checkout or git restore of a tree (not a staged-only restore), git worktree remove, Remove-Item -Recurse and its aliases, rmdir, rd, del or erase with /s, rmtree, rimraf or recursive: true, and rsync --delete. Nothing else is exempt: a scratchpad target and the guarded form ask too, and so does a command whose text only mentions a delete, the over-ask accepted. The ask's reason reaches the human, not the agent, so it is written for him and names the command. Bash builtins, sed and one grep on a pass, more on a candidate ask (about 200 ms of process time on the host it was built on, beside the push gate, since hooks on one matcher run in parallel); an EXIT trap turns every internal failure into an ask, and a hook that cannot start fails open, and so does one the 10-second timeout kills; the exemptions judge at most 40 segments and ask past that. The 10-second timeout bounds a hung start; the fixture's 300 KB command asks in about 1 second.

PreToolUse._provenance_grant_write_guard: Wires the grant-write guard onto every Bash and PowerShell call, for every caller, on the human's word. A session grant in hooks/session-roots/<session_id>.txt lets the session and its members write under a root without the path guard's foreign-root ask, and the path guard is wired on Edit|Write only, so a shell write into that folder never reached it: auto mode could pass it, and the human would never see the widening. The guard asks, never denies, when a command names session-roots, in its text or in the input's cwd, without regard to case, and carries a write shape: a redirection to a file (2>/dev/null, 2>&1, $null and NUL pass), tee, cp, mv, install, ln, dd, truncate, touch, mkdir, sed -i, perl -i, Set-Content, Add-Content, Out-File, New-Item, Copy-Item, Move-Item, Rename-Item and their aliases, [IO.File] writes, and a Python or Node file write. Reads pass (cat, ls, test -f, Get-Content, Test-Path), and so does a delete, which narrows access. It is a string heuristic against habit, not a barrier against a hand that means to hide: a path assembled at run time, an 8.3 short name, a script file the command only runs and a program writing through its own option pass. The ask's reason reaches the human, not the agent, so it is written for him and names the command. A command that never names the folder passes on Bash builtins alone; one that does costs sed, tr and one grep per shape. An EXIT trap turns every internal failure into an ask, and a hook that cannot start fails open, and so does one the 10-second timeout kills; the fixture's 300 KB command asks in about 1 second.

PreToolUse._provenance_main_session_path_guard: Wires the shared path guard onto the main session's Edit|Write in main-session mode: it asks ONLY on a proven foreign-root write (another lane's worktree, a stray external path), auto-passing everything own-root so the Lead's own-root notebook closure writes (Aim, Registry, Lanes, contract/charter surfaces) and its legitimate non-notebook writes in arbitrary projects stay frictionless. This main-session wiring is the guard file's only wiring, though the OpenKnowledge guard delegates each of its path targets to this file: the Archivist carries no path guard, its boundary (notebook surfaces, and inbox material no unit has taken up) being doctrine on its card.

PreToolUse._provenance_live_reads_guard: Wires the live-reads guard onto every Playwright and claude.ai connector tool, for every caller. A call passes silently to the ordinary permission flow only when the Operator makes it (top-level agent_type 'operator') and the tool is on the guard's read list of 24 read-shaped tools. Every other call gets an explicit ask: a write, an unlisted or future tool, an uncurated connector, a call from the main session or another agent, unparseable input. The silent pass adds no allow: in auto mode the classifier still decides the read. The exact-name write asks in permissions.ask are the second layer should this hook fail to run.

PreToolUse._provenance_openknowledge_guard: Wires the OpenKnowledge guard onto every open-knowledge tool, for every caller. Read tools pass; exec asks when a pipeline runs find with -delete or sort with -o. resolve_conflict, import, install, the skill variants of write, edit, delete, move and restore_version, and every folder delete ask for everyone. Every path a write, edit, delete, move, restore_version, checkpoint or fixing lint names is resolved through the call's own cwd, the nearest .ok/config.yml and its content.dir, then handed to guard-archivist-paths.sh main-session, so an OpenKnowledge write outside the session's root asks exactly as an Edit or Write there does, and the session grants and the Archivist's silent exit carry over. A write's asset.source outside the session's root asks, for every caller. A tool or key outside the table enumerated at OpenKnowledge 0.78.0 asks, as do a write with no .ok root, a .. segment, a batch over 100 targets and unparseable input. Four slips are denied instead, each naming the correction to resend, because a deny's reason reaches the caller and an ask's reaches only the human: a write without cwd; a cwd naming the session's root or a granted root in another letter case or the Git Bash /c/ form, where both spellings reach one folder on disk and the respelled target passes the path guard; a field a tool takes only at its top level (summary, cwd) found inside a nested object the table reads; a key of Claude Code's native file tools that no OpenKnowledge tool takes (file_path, old_string, new_string, replace_all, allow_large), at the top level or nested. A command hook that times out, crashes or exits without a decision does not block: the call goes on through the ordinary permission flow (hooks reference, Timeouts and Other exit codes). So the guard turns every internal failure into an ask through an EXIT trap, and the 600-second timeout is set explicitly rather than left to the default: a 100-target batch measured 142 s on the host it was built on, and the timeout sits about four times above that so a slow host's full batch still ends in a verdict. What neither covers: a hook that cannot start at all (bash missing) still fails open. The exact-name asks on import and install in permissions.ask are the second layer for those two tools only.

SessionStart._provenance_compaction_marker: Closes the observability gap in the context-compaction recall trigger (30-retrieval.md): a session cannot tell from inside that a compaction happened, so the trigger was unobservable. The SessionStart matcher 'compact' fires after any compaction (manual /compact or auto-compact) and injects its stdout into the model's context -- this hook writes a single ASCII marker line the retrieval rule keys on. SessionStart/compact is the injecting mechanism because PostCompact cannot inject context (side-effects only). Inline echo (not a hooks/ script) is the simplest form for a static one-line marker; ASCII-only for the PowerShell 5.1 deploy pipeline.

hooks.command: echo "[compaction-marker] This session's context was just compacted into a summary. Retrieval rule: reground the load-bearing facts the current work rests on against their surfaces before relying on them. The skills' load did not survive the summary: load writing-and-talking-style and decision-proposal-discipline again before the next thing the human reads."

SessionStart._provenance_harness_marker: Wires the harness-version marker on every session start (no matcher: startup, resume, clear, compact and fork). The hook compares the installed Claude Code version with the weighed line of the home's HARNESS.md and stays silent when they match or either is unknown. An older installed version prints one update line in any project; a newer one prints one line only where the session's cwd carries the charter of the tending that weighs each new version, at charters/harness-evolution/charter.md or notebook/tendings/harness-evolution/charter.md. Its stdout joins the session's context. The 5-second timeout bounds a hung claude --version, since a command hook otherwise waits up to 600 seconds. It exits 0 on every path and never blocks a session start.

SessionStart._provenance_session_cue: Wires the session cue on matchers startup, resume, clear, compact and fork. A runbook whose moment is only observable in the work, joining a project above all, is easy to miss without a prompt at that moment, so the hook names the load right there. It walks up from the session's cwd: a project face (notebook/Constitution.md or a root Constitution.md) prints 'load onboard before working'; the shared external brain, recognized by its root manifesto note, prints no face line; anything else prints 'ask the human before working (wrap offer)'. Every run adds 'load decision-proposal-discipline before the first ask'. On compact it skips those lines. It also carries the main-session rules when the launcher did not: without the launcher's ENSEMBLE_LEAD_APPENDED marker it prints the home's LEAD.md after one header line, on every source compact included, since hook-added text does not survive a compaction; fixtures/session-cue keeps that print under the 10,000-character hook output cap. It prints nothing when the input carries an agent_id, so a member inside a subagent never reads the main session's cue. Bash builtins only; the 5-second timeout bounds a stat on an unreachable network path. It exits 0 on every path, and a failure before the output prints nothing.

SessionStart._provenance_mod_check: Wires the mod-presence check on matchers startup, resume, clear, compact and fork. A plugin carrying a hooks module (a mod) runs inside Claude Code, and its tool.check or tool.call hook can approve a tool call past the ask rules, deny rules and guards this file wires (HARNESS.md), so the check says when one is present rather than leaving it to a glance at /plugin. It reads the home's own records and never starts a nested claude: every installPath in plugins/installed_plugins.json, the plugins under skills/ and plugins/synced/, and the folders CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS names, from the environment or from env here; and the session's own project .claude/skills/, under the cwd in its input and under CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, read once when the two name one folder, whose mods it names as ones that may load (a project skills-dir plugin loads only from the session's primary working directory, which no hook input names, and only once that folder is trusted; whether it loads under --setting-sources user is unconfirmed). A folder in skills/ or in the project's .claude/skills without .claude-plugin/plugin.json is named as one that by the docs does not load as a plugin. A plugin whose hooks/hooks.json carries a modules key is a mod; an id set false in enabledPlugins is reported as disabled, never dropped. One line per mod reaches the human through systemMessage and the session through additionalContext, which also asks the session to tell the human at its first answer; fixtures/mod-check fails a field over the 10,000-character cap. Records it cannot read, a scan past 3 seconds and any exit before a verdict print a cannot-tell line; a home with no mod prints nothing, and so does input carrying an agent_id. It cannot see a mod installed after the session started, one loaded with the --plugin-dir flag, one in a folder added with --add-dir, or one in another config home; after /cd and then a cd in the session, neither folder it reads is the one /cd moved to, which plugins load from. Unchecked: whether /clear moves the working folder back after a cd, and whether CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR reaches the hook in a session started with --setting-sources user; without it only the cwd is read. Compact is in the matcher because a mod can arrive mid-session and the check measured about 0.15 s on the host it was built on. The records reader's time grows with the square of the file: about 1 second at 100 recorded plugins on that host, and past about 200 the 3-second limit prints the cannot-tell line on a readable file; the homes it was built against record fewer than 10. Bash builtins only. The 5-second timeout ends a file test or read that blocks on an unreachable path, which the 3-second limit, checked between steps, cannot cut short; the harness then cancels the hook and discards its output (hooks reference, Timeouts), so that start carries no line from the check, the one silent failure. It exits 0 on every path.

SessionStart._provenance_refocus: Wires the stale-resume line of refocus.sh on matchers resume and fork; the script re-checks source. Claude Code 2.1.251 and later give a resumed or forked session that holds a response from Claude three fields: seconds_since_last_response, context_tokens and prompt_cache_likely_expired. When the cache has likely expired and context_tokens is at least 100,000, the hook prints one line that joins the session's context: the conversation resumed after so long idle at about so many tokens, its first request re-read the whole history, and the first reply opens with one refocus line, compact now with a stated focus while the history is cached again, or a fresh session with its resume prompt. The line arrives with the first message after the resume, which has already re-sent the history, so it serves refocus and trims later turns; it saves nothing on that first request. It is written as fact, not as an instruction, because imperative hook text can trip prompt-injection defenses. Silent on every other path, input carrying an agent_id included. The 5-second timeout bounds a hung start, since a command hook otherwise waits up to 600 seconds. It exits 0 on every path and never blocks a session start; fixtures/refocus holds its cases.

PreCompact._provenance_refocus_block: Wires the cold-compaction stop of refocus.sh on matcher manual, so only /compact reaches it; the script re-checks trigger and never blocks an automatic compaction, since blocking one can fail the request in flight. A manual /compact on a conversation whose prompt cache has expired first re-reads the whole history at full price. When the conversation has been idle longer than its cache lifetime (one hour, or five minutes when its last cache writes were 5-minute only) and its context is at least 280,000 tokens, the hook exits 2, which stops the compaction, and its stderr, which Claude Code shows the user for a manual /compact, recommends a fresh session: /clear, then name the work to pick up. The word anyway as the first word of the /compact text lets the compaction run. PreCompact input carries no idle field, so the hook reads the end of the transcript for the last main-conversation assistant line, its timestamp and its usage counts, a format Claude Code does not document (HARNESS.md); a transcript it cannot read, or a line it cannot parse, lets the compaction run. A PreCompact systemMessage is discarded, so stderr is the only channel. The 10-second timeout bounds the read of the transcript's last 8 MB, which takes under a second on a transcript over 10 MB in fixtures/refocus. It exits 0 on every path but the block.
